summary: Captain Grey and Lexy Moran, unable to get a taxi or horse, decide to walk three miles through the dark to the doctor's house to check on a woman there, since the house has no telephone. Lexy insists on accompanying him, and the two walk in tense, foreboding silence, guided by a single light in the house. The excerpt ends as they reach the front veranda and Captain Grey rings the bell.
one_line: Captain Grey and Lexy Moran walk through the dark to the doctor's house, dreading what they will find, and ring the bell.
key_facts: Lexy Moran wanted to go to the doctor's house herself, but Captain Grey insisted on going first to see how the woman there was.
Mr. Binz suggested that someone should come all the way out to the house, but Lexy cried 'Oh, all right!' impatiently.
The doctor's house has no telephone, which is why Captain Grey proposed going there in person.
Captain Grey said, 'If there's no change, I'll come back.'
Lexy insisted on going with Captain Grey, saying 'If you will go, I'm going with you!'
Joe's taxi was not available at the garage because Joe and his taxi had gone out.
An interested bystander said a 'rig' could be obtained from the livery stable with no trouble.
Captain Grey declined the rig, saying 'I can't wait' and that he would walk.
The walk to the doctor's house is described as three miles.
Lexy had already walked that three miles once earlier that day and had walked farther with Houseman in the afternoon.
The pair walked down a lane, leaving the highway lights behind, in thick darkness under the trees.
The sound of the sea was described as 'the loneliest sound in all the world.'
Lexy said 'There's a light in the house, anyhow!' and Captain Grey answered 'Naturally!' with a trace of impatience.
Their footsteps on the gravel drive sounded as sharp as pistol shots when they mounted the veranda.
Captain Grey rang the bell at the front door of the house.
